payload.acceptance_criteria:
A consumer in [[release.consumers]] can name parallel CI groups, and consumer-proof runs the commands of each group at the same time on its core set.
The proof fails when any group fails, and the result names the failing group.
handily's ci list in basicly.toml runs its mods test suite in 4 shards, and a live proof of handily finishes in under 6 minutes on cores 16-31.
payload.description:
## Context
When a basicly release is cut, I want the consumer proof to take less time, so the proof fits the 10-minute release target. A parallel proof measured 848 s on 2026-11-19, and handily's own suite took about 14 min of it. Orchestrator decision 2026-11-19 19:06 UTC: run the proof before the release window now (option b), and file sharding as a P2 follow-up (option a).
payload.title: Shard a consumer's suite inside the consumer proof

## Context
When pipe-status-guard refuses a command, I want its advice to name the Code Mode REPL form, so an agent in a REPL script keeps the command's own status. The narrowing first ordered (Orchestrator 2026-11-19 11:06 UTC) was dropped after three council runs found leaks each time (Orchestrator 18:42 UTC): the guard's logic stays as on main. Lane: harness/dev-pipe-advice.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
The refusal advice gives the Code Mode REPL form: cut the output in JavaScript, so .exitCode stays the command's status.
The 5 true refusals of the 2026-11-19 investigation are test cases and stay refused.
The guard's refusal logic is unchanged from main: every earlier test of pipe-status-guard still passes.
